answer: Commit-reveal spot audits deter sybils: at admission each seat seals a hash of a unique storage sector plus a bond, a commitment hard as onyx it cannot later swap. Every epoch a public random beacon names a few seats to reveal the preimage and serve a freshly challenged slice; a clone that merely copied a neighbor's hash has no matching secret and no real timber beneath it, so one failed reveal sends its bond into a slashing spiral. Running N fakes means N distinct sectors held idle and N standing audit risks, not one cheap row.
